shorts.title: Start Before You're Ready
shorts.angle: Taking action instead of waiting for perfect conditions. One idea: every week you wait, you learn nothing.
shorts.hook: I started contacting customers before my tools were ready.
shorts.voiceover:
I started contacting customers before my tools were ready.
Not because I was confident. Because every week I waited, I learned nothing.
So I picked a small group of real people and sent the first message. [FILL: only if true, otherwise say: "So I'm picking a small group of real people to message."]
Then I built the tool to keep track of it. A to-do list. A follow-up date. A place to write down what happened.
You don't need the perfect plan to start. You need the next small step, and somewhere to record what happens.
I'm Andrew. I'm building a business, and the software to run it. Follow along.

shorts.screen_recording_requirements: A12, A18 and A17 (captured by me, DEMO DATA). B02 and B06 are yours: a real first message being written/sent (recipient and message hidden) and a desk shot. If B02 does not exist yet, the edit uses a slate.
shorts.captions: Burn-in, 2 lines max, 5-6 words a line, white on dark rounded box, highlight colour on the key word of each line. Safe zone: keep captions between 18% and 70% of the height so the app UI does not cover them.
shorts.editing: Cut every 2-4 seconds. First 1.5 seconds: the hook text on screen with the first spoken words. No music for the first line, a low bed after. Duck music 12 dB under the voice. Keep the DEMO DATA label visible on every captured product clip.

shorts.title: Building the Tool I Need
shorts.angle: Building software around a real business problem: outreach gets messy and forgetting is the failure mode.
shorts.hook: Outreach gets messy fast. Who did I message? Who needs a follow-up?
shorts.voiceover:
Outreach gets messy fast.
Who did I message? What did I say? Who needs a follow-up today?
If the answer lives in your head, you will forget.
So I'm building the tool that answers it. This is my Today screen. Follow-ups due. Who replied. What to do next.
Every business has a stage in the pipeline, and a full history I can step through, event by event.
It doesn't send anything for me, and it doesn't guess. It records what I do, and shows me what I recorded.
I'm building it around my own outreach, and I'll tell you if it works. Andrew Builds.

shorts.title: Two Businesses, One Experiment
shorts.angle: Testing whether you can build a business and a sellable software product at the same time, with honest odds.
shorts.hook: One experiment. Two businesses. No guarantees.
shorts.voiceover:
One experiment. Two businesses. No guarantees.
Business one: I'm reaching out to real companies and trying to win paying customers.
Business two: the software I'm building to run that outreach. If it genuinely helps me, it might become a product for other people.
Right now? The software has one user: me. And [FILL: your verified revenue, or "I haven't made a dollar from this yet"].
That's the experiment. If the first business works, the tool earns its place. If the tool works, it might become a second business.
Follow along and watch whether either one does. I'm Andrew.
